causal_chain.mechanism:
The protected operation is admission of a semantically distinct job to the queue. At affected release 2.3.0 (f19385d2dfc9a9496fffb01f3b2daf163ab43eae), QueueManager::push resolves an application job class with App::className and rejects an unknown class. It obtains a queue configuration and checks the job's static shouldBeUnique property. A missing uniqueness-cache configuration raises an exception. Only then does it call getUniqueId(class, method, data). A truthy Cache::read causes an immediate return **before** ClientMessage construction and sendEvent. After sending an admitted message, it stores that same identifier with Cache::add.

getUniqueId takes the array by value, calls sort($data), JSON encodes the resulting values, concatenates class/method/JSON and hashes with MD5. Sorting discards associative keys and reindexes values; it also discards positional order. Consequently, distinct job parameters can map to the same canonical input before hashing. This is a lossy comparison, not evidence of a cryptanalytic MD5 collision. The original unmodified data still goes into the queued message, so keys and positions can matter to the actual job even though the duplicate check ignores them. Message::getArgument returns that data (or the legacy args[0] representation), and Processor::processMessage passes the Message to the selected job callable. A suppressed job never reaches that consumer.

Required conditions are an application path that lets a user influence relevant job data, a job with shouldBeUnique enabled, the same resolved class/method and cache namespace, and a previously admitted job's matching cache entry that has not yet been cleared or expired. The library itself supplies no universal unauthenticated HTTP endpoint. The advisory's unauthenticated network classification therefore depends on the integrating application. The user need not control the job class or cache implementation to influence its data. Impact is loss of legitimate queued work, rather than demonstrated disclosure or code execution. There is no claim that every installation exposes this path.

The cache defaults to a 24-hour duration if configured without an override. Normal worker result handling recomputes the unique ID from Message::getArgument and deletes it. The cache entry's lifetime and worker progress constrain the suppression window; no permanent outage or measured resource-exhaustion claim is made. At 2.3.0 and 2.3.1, per-configuration uniqueCacheKey connects push and worker cleanup. Resource allocation is not the reported mechanism.

Counterevidence and legitimate use: ignoring genuinely identical queued work is the feature's intended idempotency behavior, explicitly documented in the introducing change and PR #108. The failure is collapsing semantically different data into that identity. Jobs without shouldBeUnique bypass this check, matching the advisory workaround of application-managed idempotency. Invalid class or missing cache configuration does not reach the vulnerable admission path. The source supports conditional exposure, not arbitrary dropping of jobs across every class or installation.

Evidence: evidence/detailed-history.stdout contains the exact parent, child and release QueueManager, Message, Processor and cleanup sources. evidence/final-observations.stdout contains line-numbered QueueManager and WorkerCommand for 0.1.10, 0.1.11, 2.3.0 and 2.3.1. evidence/repair-integration.stdout retains WorkerCommand wiring and Message behavior. These are static source observations. No PHP regression, exploit, broker or end-to-end job execution occurred.

## Finding

**NOT_AI under the frozen evidence threshold.** The advisory describes a real conditional availability defect in cakephp/queue: value sorting erases the semantic identity of job parameters before uniqueness checking, allowing a different job to be suppressed as an existing duplicate. The causal change is named-human-authored unique-job support, not an AI-attributed change. This conclusion is scoped to recovered public source, metadata and contemporaneous disclosure evidence; it does not prove undisclosed AI use impossible.

The earliest affected published source release is **0.1.11**, not the GHSA range's 0.1.10. The minimum repairing member is **13890591e248acc8824becb24ba1939fa061bd34**; first default-branch closure is its integration **4a9d77a4865896a8464318f36962e107a0757b22**, which is also the **2.3.1** tag. These are separate causal roles. No source-bound evidence establishes AI participation in either the introducing change or the repair.

## A. Advisory identity and status

Keyed official identifier: CVE-2026-54713. Its live CVE JSON has the matching cveMetadata.cveId and state PUBLISHED, normalized to ACTIVE. The matching GHSA-r5pm-vrc5-3m73 global advisory has published_at 2026-08-27T17:03:56Z and an explicitly null withdrawn_at, also ACTIVE. Its identifiers bind the two aliases. Neither is rejected or withdrawn; ordinary aliasing is not duplicate exclusion. NVD's Deferred describes enrichment status, not rejection. The CVE publication time is 2026-08-27T17:03:31.580Z, later than repair shipment.

The retained GHSA and the fresh GHSA both claim >=0.1.10,<2.3.1. Retained NVD and the CVE describe >=0.1.11,<2.3.1. This is a lower-bound discrepancy settled by source content in section F, not grounds for rejecting the vulnerability.

Live receipts preserve exact authoritative URLs. evidence/final-observations.stdout verifies both retained input hashes against SOURCES.json.

## B. Mechanism, authority and counterevidence

The protected operation is admission of a semantically distinct job to the queue. At affected release 2.3.0 (f19385d2dfc9a9496fffb01f3b2daf163ab43eae), QueueManager::push resolves an application job class with App::className and rejects an unknown class. It obtains a queue configuration and checks the job's static shouldBeUnique property. A missing uniqueness-cache configuration raises an exception. Only then does it call getUniqueId(class, method, data). A truthy Cache::read causes an immediate return **before** ClientMessage construction and sendEvent. After sending an admitted message, it stores that same identifier with Cache::add.

getUniqueId takes the array by value, calls sort($data), JSON encodes the resulting values, concatenates class/method/JSON and hashes with MD5. Sorting discards associative keys and reindexes values; it also discards positional order. Consequently, distinct job parameters can map to the same canonical input before hashing. This is a lossy comparison, not evidence of a cryptanalytic MD5 collision. The original unmodified data still goes into the queued message, so keys and positions can matter to the actual job even though the duplicate check ignores them. Message::getArgument returns that data (or the legacy args[0] representation), and Processor::processMessage passes the Message to the selected job callable. A suppressed job never reaches that consumer.

Required conditions are an application path that lets a user influence relevant job data, a job with shouldBeUnique enabled, the same resolved class/method and cache namespace, and a previously admitted job's matching cache entry that has not yet been cleared or expired. The library itself supplies no universal unauthenticated HTTP endpoint. The advisory's unauthenticated network classification therefore depends on the integrating application. The user need not control the job class or cache implementation to influence its data. Impact is loss of legitimate queued work, rather than demonstrated disclosure or code execution. There is no claim that every installation exposes this path.

The cache defaults to a 24-hour duration if configured without an override. Normal worker result handling recomputes the unique ID from Message::getArgument and deletes it. The cache entry's lifetime and worker progress constrain the suppression window; no permanent outage or measured resource-exhaustion claim is made. At 2.3.0 and 2.3.1, per-configuration uniqueCacheKey connects push and worker cleanup. Resource allocation is not the reported mechanism.

Counterevidence and legitimate use: ignoring genuinely identical queued work is the feature's intended idempotency behavior, explicitly documented in the introducing change and PR #108. The failure is collapsing semantically different data into that identity. Jobs without shouldBeUnique bypass this check, matching the advisory workaround of application-managed idempotency. Invalid class or missing cache configuration does not reach the vulnerable admission path. The source supports conditional exposure, not arbitrary dropping of jobs across every class or installation.

Evidence: evidence/detailed-history.stdout contains the exact parent, child and release QueueManager, Message, Processor and cleanup sources. evidence/final-observations.stdout contains line-numbered QueueManager and WorkerCommand for 0.1.10, 0.1.11, 2.3.0 and 2.3.1. evidence/repair-integration.stdout retains WorkerCommand wiring and Message behavior. The keyed GHSA is `reviewed`, has no `withdrawn_at`, and the repository advisory
endpoint returns `state: published` (`published_at 2026-09-16T14:17:24Z`,
`withdrawn_at null`) — evidence/repo-advisory.json. CVE-2026-91129 is public
(vulnStatus "Awaiting Analysis", CWE-918). Neither alias is rejected, withdrawn or a
duplicate, so this is not a FALSE_POSITIVE by advisory disposition; the stated mechanism
is also affirmatively corroborated (below), so `MECHANISM_REFUTED` does not apply.

## 1. Mechanism — SSRF via unauthenticated mDNS and redirect-following shared client
Chain: a local-network attacker multicasts a crafted mDNS response advertising a fake
`_ipp._tcp.local` service (port 5353). Home Assistant's zeroconf layer routes it to the
IPP config flow. `async_step_zeroconf` (evidence/ipp-config_flow-at-815c708.py) reads
`discovery_info.host`, `.port`, `.type` and `properties["rp"]` from that unauthenticated
announcement with no validation and stores them as `CONF_HOST`/`CONF_PORT`/
`CONF_BASE_PATH`; it then immediately `await`s `validate_input`, which builds
`IPP(host=..., port=..., base_path=..., session=async_get_clientsession(hass))` and calls
`await ipp.printer()` — no user interaction, no prior IPP configuration. `async_get_clientsession`
returns HA's shared `aiohttp.ClientSession`, which accepted redirects; a `302 Location:
http://127.0.0.1:<port>/...` from the attacker host was therefore followed, coercing HA
into an authenticated-context request to loopback/internal services (AV:A/PR:N/UI:N,
C:L/I:L/A:N, CVSS 5.4). The reported failure is thus a *design* SSRF: untrusted discovery
data reaching an outbound request through a client that did not restrict loopback
redirects. Counterevidence considered: the IPP discovery itself is intentional and the
fetch of the advertised device is expected; the defect is only the unchecked
cross-origin redirect to internal addresses (relative redirects and requests already
targeting loopback are legitimate and were left working by the fix).

## 2. BIC and landing
The invariant that fails is enforced in the shared client: "a request issued to a
non-loopback host must not be redirected to a loopback/unspecified target." The object
that first introduces HA's shared aiohttp clientsession — the exact layer the repair
modifies — is `cf57db919e450d2898a079fb9beb5467663de256` ("Refactory aiohttp clientsession
handling in HA (#4602)", 2016-11-28, author Pascal Vizeli <pascal.vizeli@syshack.ch>,
parent `84b12ab0078ed95a4bc3de67e088027ebd919d1f`), which created
`homeassistant/helpers/aiohttp_client.py`. Granularity ATOMIC; the introducer is on the
default branch, so `landing_commit` is null (`INTRODUCER_ON_DEFAULT`). The full 96-commit
path history (evidence/hist-aiohttp_full.json) shows no origin/redirect restriction was
ever present before the fix, so the client never had this invariant.
Exposing consumer, recorded separately from the introducer: `98f68f4798ae91668d63caefb484f690628adba5`
("Add IPP integration (#32859)", 2020-03-30, Chris Talkington) added the automatic
zeroconf `validate_input` probe that is the trigger path. This is the alternative
candidate BIC; it is a later exposure of the same client design and is retained in
`candidate_set`, not used as `introducer_sha`. Both candidate origins predate capable
LLM coding agents (2016 / 2020), which independently bounds AI involvement in the origin.

`fix_sha` = `815c708d19aa0c7f59f9ee318b613a5e481a42b3` ("Block redirect to localhost
(#162941)", author Robert Resch <robert@resch.dev>, merged to default branch `dev`
2026-02-13, PR merge_commit_sha = same, labels include `cherry-picked`). The repair adds
`_ssrf_redirect_middleware` to `_async_create_clientsession`; on a 3xx response from a

loopback (`localhost`, `*.localhost`, `localhost.`) or unspecified IPs, while leaving
relative redirects, non-network schemes and loopback origins unaffected

landing `0f3c7ca2772b605c0f3c09c88f35e527ea6ea560` (committer Franck Nijhof, 2026-02-20,

enforcement to resume-refused protocols — informational, not the closure. No AI marker was
found on either the fix object or its backport (committers GitHub bot / Franck Nijhof,
author Robert Resch).

`introducer_sha` `cf57db919e45...` carries a recovered named human identity (Pascal Vizeli
<pascal.vizeli@syshack.ch>, committer Paulus Schoutsen) with no agent/bot author, no
AI co-author trailer and no first-person AI disclosure; it is from 2016, before capable
LLM coding assistants existed. The alternative exposing path `98f68f4798ae` is likewise
human (Chris Talkington, 2020) with no marker. HA's contemporaneous PR template says
"AI tools are welcome, but contributors are responsible for *fully* understanding the code
before submitting a PR" and lists "Any generated code has been carefully reviewed"
(evidence/PR_TEMPLATE.md) — a policy that *mentions* AI rather than mandating disclosure,
recorded as `POLICY_MENTIONS_AI`. Scope/limitation: this "no marker" statement was made by
reading GitHub REST commit/trailer metadata, not by enumerating every local commit object

research sidecar. Since every candidate causal object predates LLM agents, the verdict does
not depend on that enumeration.

GHSA vulnerable range `< 2026.2.2`, first patched `2026.2.3`; NVD/CVE says affected

carrier text, not an open surface (`residual_triage: NOT-RESIDUAL`).
`flip_condition`: a first-party object that carries the causal content AND an AI
agent/bot author, AI co-author trailer, or first-person AI disclosure bound to that

behavior was authored by an AI tool) would move the verdict to `AI_ROOT_CAUSE`/`AI_CODE_FLAWED`;

commit. A local commit-object enumeration showing an AI trailer on a pre-force-push
iteration of the same causal blob would also flip it.

sibling `evidence/` files. Schema/checks support delivery, not truth.

# Independent audit — alias-cf30e848d5a28fda1cdc7e96

Class: `alias-cf30e848d5a28fda1cdc7e96` · repository mapping lead: `home-assistant/core`
Aliases: `GHSA-4GHV-53CQ-7WP3`, `CVE-2026-91129` · contract `2026-09-27.3`, research-work `causal-work-v1`
Verdict: **NOT_AI** (advisory ACTIVE). Attempt 1, auditor2, endpoint research.

## 0. Advisory status — ACTIVE
The keyed GHSA is `reviewed`, has no `withdrawn_at`, and the repository advisory
endpoint returns `state: published` (`published_at 2026-09-16T14:17:24Z`,
`withdrawn_at null`) — evidence/repo-advisory.json. CVE-2026-91129 is public
(vulnStatus "Awaiting Analysis", CWE-918). Neither alias is rejected, withdrawn or a
duplicate, so this is not a FALSE_POSITIVE by advisory disposition; the stated mechanism
is also affirmatively corroborated (below), so `MECHANISM_REFUTED` does not apply.

## 1. Mechanism — SSRF via unauthenticated mDNS and redirect-following shared client
Chain: a local-network attacker multicasts a crafted mDNS response advertising a fake
`_ipp._tcp.local` service (port 5353). Home Assistant's zeroconf layer routes it to the
IPP config flow. `async_step_zeroconf` (evidence/ipp-config_flow-at-815c708.py) reads
`discovery_info.host`, `.port`, `.type` and `properties["rp"]` from that unauthenticated
announcement with no validation and stores them as `CONF_HOST`/`CONF_PORT`/
`CONF_BASE_PATH`; it then immediately `await`s `validate_input`, which builds
`IPP(host=..., port=..., base_path=..., session=async_get_clientsession(hass))` and calls
`await ipp.printer()` — no user interaction, no prior IPP configuration. `async_get_clientsession`
returns HA's shared `aiohttp.ClientSession`, which accepted redirects; a `302 Location:
http://127.0.0.1:<port>/...` from the attacker host was therefore followed, coercing HA
into an authenticated-context request to loopback/internal services (AV:A/PR:N/UI:N,
C:L/I:L/A:N, CVSS 5.4). The reported failure is thus a *design* SSRF: untrusted discovery
data reaching an outbound request through a client that did not restrict loopback
redirects. Counterevidence considered: the IPP discovery itself is intentional and the
fetch of the advertised device is expected; the defect is only the unchecked
cross-origin redirect to internal addresses (relative redirects and requests already
targeting loopback are legitimate and were left working by the fix).

## 2. BIC and landing
The invariant that fails is enforced in the shared client: "a request issued to a
non-loopback host must not be redirected to a loopback/unspecified target." The object
that first introduces HA's shared aiohttp clientsession — the exact layer the repair
modifies — is `cf57db919e450d2898a079fb9beb5467663de256` ("Refactory aiohttp clientsession
handling in HA (#4602)", 2016-11-28, author Pascal Vizeli <pascal.vizeli@syshack.ch>,
parent `84b12ab0078ed95a4bc3de67e088027ebd919d1f`), which created
`homeassistant/helpers/aiohttp_client.py`. Granularity ATOMIC; the introducer is on the
default branch, so `landing_commit` is null (`INTRODUCER_ON_DEFAULT`). The full 96-commit
path history (evidence/hist-aiohttp_full.json) shows no origin/redirect restriction was
ever present before the fix, so the client never had this invariant.
Exposing consumer, recorded separately from the introducer: `98f68f4798ae91668d63caefb484f690628adba5`
("Add IPP integration (#32859)", 2020-03-30, Chris Talkington) added the automatic
zeroconf `validate_input` probe that is the trigger path. This is the alternative
candidate BIC; it is a later exposure of the same client design and is retained in
`candidate_set`, not used as `introducer_sha`. Both candidate origins predate capable
LLM coding agents (2016 / 2020), which independently bounds AI involvement in the origin.

## 3. Repair and release
`fix_sha` = `815c708d19aa0c7f59f9ee318b613a5e481a42b3` ("Block redirect to localhost
(#162941)", author Robert Resch <robert@resch.dev>, merged to default branch `dev`
2026-02-13, PR merge_commit_sha = same, labels include `cherry-picked`). The repair adds
`_ssrf_redirect_middleware` to `_async_create_clientsession`; on a 3xx response from a
non-loopback origin it resolves the `Location` host and raises `SSRFRedirectError` for
loopback (`localhost`, `*.localhost`, `localhost.`) or unspecified IPs, while leaving
relative redirects, non-network schemes and loopback origins unaffected
(evidence/fix-0f3c7ca.patch). This closes the reported mechanism because the redirect to
`127.0.0.1` is refused before the second request is issued. The cherry-picked release-branch
landing `0f3c7ca2772b605c0f3c09c88f35e527ea6ea560` (committer Franck Nijhof, 2026-02-20,
parent `3abf7c22...`) is the *other landing* of the same repair (`fix_shas`) and shipped in

An application must actually give it untrusted data; the package is not itself an exposed network service and no deployed application's reachability was assumed.

Before the repair it then reads `values[index]` without an upper bound. The violated invariant is that cache indices should correspond to the current serialized values table. Authorization to choose serialized data does not imply authority to choose arbitrary backing-store growth for the parser's bookkeeping.

The requested initial array length is N, the number of values-table entries. That is distinct from its allocated backing-store capacity. A later indexed assignment can extend the JavaScript array length and trigger engine-dependent dense/dictionary representation changes. Each parse gets a new local cache; it is reused during that call, then becomes eligible for collection when the call and any retaining trusted callbacks no longer hold it. There is no cache-size accounting or parse-time CPU quota in the inspected default path. Normal serializer output references table entries and uses cache reuse for shared values/cycles. Engine maximum lengths and conversion heuristics remain in force; requested logical length must not be equated with eagerly allocated bytes. Repeated requests repeat parsing and allocation work; this is an availability allegation, not a demonstrated persistent memory leak.

No malicious input, resource-exhaustion sequence, representation-transition benchmark or exploit was executed. ## Finding

**NOT_AI under this contract's attribution threshold.** The advisory describes a real missing bound in devalue's hydration cache, exposed when an application parses untrusted serialized values. The causal change is the recursive hydration rewrite in `1e661a47a933de9e6dde94c13552b036f55e045c`, authored and committed by Rich Harris on 2022-10-03. Its immediate parent does not perform attacker-indexed writes into a separate hydration array. Its metadata contains no AI disclosure. Repair `8b2a4562c446d7c36d9d629778079a5fae4243e1` rejects indices at or beyond the values table's length before reading the value and writing the cache. ## Mechanism and security boundary

At v5.9.1 / fix parent `3e01a6c749e215e16c94f5c132f46f7840dfa5e0`, the exported `parse(serialized, revivers, options)` calls `JSON.parse` and passes its result to exported `unflatten`. The default path accepts a nonempty array, sets `values` to that parsed table, allocates `hydrated = Array(values.length)`, and begins at index zero. A normal serialized container contains references to other table entries. Set, Map, ordinary-array, null-prototype-object and ordinary-object branches feed those references to `hydrate`. This is a real public library entry point, not an unused helper or a test-only caller. An application must actually give it untrusted data; the package is not itself an exposed network service and no deployed application's reachability was assumed.

`hydrate` first handles the five special negative primitive sentinels, rejects standalone nonsentinel values and nonnumeric references, and reuses already cached entries. Before the repair it then reads `values[index]` without an upper bound. An out-of-table ordinary numeric index yields undefined; the primitive branch still executes `hydrated[index] = ops.fromPrimitive(value)`. The default operation returns the primitive unchanged. Thus attacker-selected numeric references become numeric writes into the local JavaScript array even when they are not references to any serialized value. The violated invariant is that cache indices should correspond to the current serialized values table. Authorization to choose serialized data does not imply authority to choose arbitrary backing-store growth for the parser's bookkeeping.

The requested initial array length is N, the number of values-table entries. That is distinct from its allocated backing-store capacity. A later indexed assignment can extend the JavaScript array length and trigger engine-dependent dense/dictionary representation changes. Each parse gets a new local cache; it is reused during that call, then becomes eligible for collection when the call and any retaining trusted callbacks no longer hold it. There is no cache-size accounting or parse-time CPU quota in the inspected default path. Normal serializer output references table entries and uses cache reuse for shared values/cycles. Merely choosing an out-of-table index gives no additional legitimate serialized value.

The first-party advisory reports quadratic work from alternating array representations. Independent static inspection of V8 12.4.254 supports the underlying cost mechanism: js-objects.cc `ShouldConvertToFastElements` compares dictionary capacity against array length/new capacity; `AddDataElement` chooses dictionary or fast storage and can extend array length. elements.cc `ConvertElementsWithCapacity` allocates a new backing array and copies elements. These are potentially capacity-proportional operations, not constant-cost index validation. Engine maximum lengths and conversion heuristics remain in force; requested logical length must not be equated with eagerly allocated bytes. Repeated requests repeat parsing and allocation work; this is an availability allegation, not a demonstrated persistent memory leak.

No malicious input, resource-exhaustion sequence, representation-transition benchmark or exploit was executed. The exact quadratic scaling and thresholds are retained as the maintainer's report, supported by the inspected write path and engine conversion machinery, not as a new measurement or a universal complexity claim for every JavaScript engine. The source evidence is sufficient for the bounded missing-validation finding and its repair. Runtime-specific magnitude would require separate permitted performance evidence; this attempt does not create an operational payload to obtain it.

## Finding

**NOT_AI under the frozen attribution threshold. The vulnerability itself is supported.** A verified ordinary user can persist their own chat history with cyclic string identifiers. Deleting a message can leave a cycle reachable by a synchronous, unguarded child-link descent. That descent cannot terminate, starving the affected worker's event loop. The default startup script runs one worker, supporting a default-deployment availability impact. This is a source-based conclusion, not an independently executed denial-of-service demonstration.

The smallest recovered causal change is `22a44e67a8ba781feb8f2a267fed0c40213d8432`, authored by Timothy Jaeryang Baek `<tim@openwebui.com>`. Its complete metadata has no AI disclosure. It introduces explicit message deletion and its traversal together. The contemporaneous PR template mentions AI review policy, but does not attribute this change to AI. All local commit objects were enumerated and the relevant historical path examined; AI-marked descendants carrying unchanged vulnerable content were separated from changes to that content or its exposure. No supported AI contribution to this defect was found. This protocol verdict does not claim to exclude undisclosed AI assistance.

The original repairing member is `2bd7f24d21591060e074a90f25df8bac087a2911`; its squash landing on `dev` is `b933292d63d12be3fd1416fe55519ddc7aa336bc`. First closure on the default branch is **`d3e8bf3405e848cfba377814d0aa7ba7290e414d`**, the 0.11.1 integration. These are distinct roles. Stable source tags 0.10.0, 0.10.1, 0.10.2 and 0.11.0 contain the identical unguarded helper; 0.11.1 contains the guard. The preceding 0.9.6 tag lacks the helper.

## Advisory identity and lifecycle

The keyed advisory is CVE-2026-88000. The live CVE record has matching `cveMetadata.cveId` and `state: PUBLISHED`; its CNA identifies open-webui and links GHSA-3cgp-3cqx-j8w2. The matching global GitHub advisory has `published_at: 2026-09-09T23:54:22Z` and explicit `withdrawn_at: null`, so both are ACTIVE. No withdrawn/rejected alias was observed. The retained NVD record says Analyzed, separately from publication lifecycle. Its version range agrees with the GHSA and CVE CNA.

Evidence: `sources/cve-current.json`, `sources/ghsa-current.json`, their paired `receipts/*.json` and HTTP headers; original assigned snapshots and provenance are copied as `sources/retained-*`. Fresh HTTP responses were successful. The GHSA description supplies the reported runtime measurements; this audit does not adopt them as its own measurements.

## Mechanism and authority

At affected repair-parent `f100edb70874808c93fab84eae1810595f9e9dc3`, `backend/open_webui/main.py:824` mounts the chats router at `/api/v1/chats`. `ChatForm` in `models/chats.py:230` accepts a dictionary, without a tree/acyclicity schema. The `/new` handler in `routers/chats.py:775` uses `get_verified_user`, then `Chats.insert_new_chat`. `utils/auth.py:497` allows roles `user` and `admin`. A folder-access check only applies when a folder is requested. No special privilege is needed for an ordinary user's own chat.

`insert_new_chat` at model line 492 stores a cleaned copy of the submitted dictionary, commits it, then performs a best-effort message-table dual write. Cleaning removes null bytes; it does not rebuild child links or enforce graph invariants. JSON represents this graph with message-ID strings, not recursive in-memory objects, so ordinary JSON serialization does not reject graph cycles. `merge_history` rebuilds child lists on an update path but is not used by creation. The persisted JSON remains the deletion helper's authoritative input; normalized message-table contents do not replace that input.

The `DELETE /{id}/messages/{message_id}` handler at router line 1497 loads the chat, checks owner or admin, and calls `delete_message_from_chat_by_id_and_message_id`. Ownership restricts whose chat can be modified but does not prevent a user from constructing the offending structure in their own chat. The model method at line 1101 sanitizes null bytes and calls `_repair_chat_current_id`, then synchronously calls `delete_message_from_history` at line 1113, inside the async request path. The current-ID repair does not validate or remove child-link cycles. Its optional `_last_descendant_id` walk is separately guarded; a normal valid current message without a context summary returns before that optional walk.

The deletion helper at lines 872–910 removes the selected message and its immediate children, reparents grandchildren, then starts at the removed message's parent and repeatedly follows the last child identifier. If that remaining relation leads back to an already visited message, the same finite state recurs forever: the loop neither mutates the remaining links nor records visits. This establishes the reported recurrence statically. A valid acyclic conversation instead ends at an empty child list. The invariant at issue is termination for every stored history reachable through an authorized product operation.

The spinning loop performs dictionary lookups and assignments with no await, cancellation checkpoint, allocation growth, or work budget. It therefore prevents the affected asyncio worker from handling other requests, including its health route. Existing request/session allocations stay live while CPU work continues; this is not a claim of growing memory use. The startup script defaults `UVICORN_WORKERS` to 1, also verified at the 0.11.0 source tag. Multiple-worker or replicated deployments require a narrower conclusion: one request blocks its selected worker; this inspection does not prove every worker or replica stalls. Request disconnects cannot be acted on by the blocked loop until it yields. The helper mutates an in-memory copy before database commit; a hang occurs before the deletion commit. The vulnerability claim is availability loss, not unauthorized disclosure. Ordinary successful deletion intentionally changes the user's chat.

Evidence: `sources/parent-chats.py`, `parent-router.py`, `parent-main.py`, `parent-auth.py`, `parent-start.sh`, `v0.11.0-start.sh`; each has a URL/HTTP/hash receipt. The immediate parent has neither `delete_message_from_history` nor the explicit deletion endpoint. The child adds both, changes history updates to merge existing messages, and removes inference of deletion from omitted IDs. The member landed on main through `4d2e13cf2bcc451b33bb6374bea4d2163e6cc94c` (PR 26385 / 0.10.0). The landing is not the introducer. Local ancestry and metadata are retained in `receipts/final-observations.json` and `final-observation-2.txt`; associated PR metadata is in `sources/introduction-prs.json`. Source extraction binds the member and landing to the identical helper SHA-256 `24566cb8b3ddc9941fbcb31d0fbe0739bfbefff526aa39dc9aec157ddb3f9502`. This is an actual function-content comparison, not attribution from a PR number. The repository is non-shallow; no root/import boundary or unreconstructable aggregate was needed.

Tree traversal examined `backend/open_webui/models/chats.py`, found 165 distinct blobs, and read all 165 without missing content. There were 938 exact matches for the vulnerable helper. Every matching commit's complete metadata is retained in `receipts/carrier-metadata.txt`; the object/path universe, function digest and matches are in `receipts/local-object-universe.txt` and `carrier-analysis.json`. A later bounded repair-member fetch added exactly one commit, `2bd7f24d21591060e074a90f25df8bac087a2911`, whose full metadata and repairing patch were separately inspected; final enumeration is retained in `local-object-universe-final.txt`.

Twenty-four matches had AI-related marker candidates. Their full metadata and changed paths were inspected (`receipts/marker-scope.json` and individual `marker-*.txt`). They retain pre-existing vulnerable helper content while changing other operations. They do not attribute the original helper to AI merely by containing it. Two plausible indirect candidates received patch inspection: `c882222f68fed329705e028d4316f460b33b2cd0` adds ownership checks to chat-completed/actions, not to chat creation or message deletion; this case already requires ownership and therefore is not an omission of that ownership invariant. `8d6a7c8308c507f40466993732dbbd3c6930d04a` changes JSON engine serialization, preserving ordinary string-ID structure; it does not introduce graph acceptance that was previously prevented. See `sources/ai-ownership.patch` and `ai-json.patch`.

The separately cycle-guarded `_last_descendant_id` originated in `5caa91a49304148696641d1cd39e43184ba8d748`, also named Timothy Jaeryang Baek without an AI marker (`receipts/descendant-history.txt`, `sources/descendant-hardening.patch`). Both the original repair member and its dev squash have no AI marker in their own complete metadata. Aggregate main-branch merge attribution is not assigned to a hunk.

Coverage is bounded to public primary material and the actual local object inventory, not inaccessible deleted remote history or private author activity. The promisor clone's configuration is disclosed, but all blobs in the enumerated historical causal path were present. No missing clone content was treated as evidence of no AI use.

The minimum repair initializes `visited_ids`, checks the next identifier against it in the while condition, and adds each traversed identifier. With stable finite stored JSON, each existing identifier can be followed at most once; a missing child ends at an empty lookup. Malformed types may raise ordinary errors; this patch proves closure of the reported infinite cycle descent, not universal acceptance or sanitization of every malformed chat. The set has storage proportional to traversed identifiers. Surrounding deletion work still processes submitted child/grandchild lists, but there is no self-repeating traversal after this guard. Old stored cycles need no migration for this particular loop to terminate.

Its first-parent history shows the 0.11.1 integration `d3e8bf3405e848cfba377814d0aa7ba7290e414d`, whose first parent `01f4282f1ffe0d6212f58d3afbeae21fffd0c4be` still has the vulnerable helper. That negative ancestry result is exit 1 by design, not a retrieval failure.

`receipts/version-source-reads.json` records exact Git show commands, full commit and blob IDs, source hashes, and helper hashes for each compared revision and source tag. `sources/releases.json` supplies official tag names, publication dates, and prerelease flags. 0.11.1 is a stable release published 2026-08-25T21:17:57Z; its tag resolves to the main-branch integration. The actual release router still invokes the repaired model method (`sources/release-router.py`), and release startup defaults retain the expected worker setup. Verified version claims concern these official source trees; this audit did not inspect every wheel, container, platform build or deployment.

An isolated ordinary regression check extracts only the helper AST from 0.11.0 and 0.11.1. Missing-message, leaf, middle, root and single-message deletions produce the same expected outputs before and after repair: ten assertions/checks passed. `receipts/ordinary-regression.txt` and its command receipt preserve the result. No cyclic histories, server execution, or exploit test occurred. Termination for cycles is a static proof from the guard, not a dynamic result.

Execution failures are preserved separately from research findings. The initial history walk caused Git automatic packing to fail with “unable to create thread: Resource temporarily unavailable”; the raw `gc.log` is saved as `receipts/git-gc-failure.txt`. # Independent audit: alias-06ed0ff27b4c5774babfe180

Task: agentic-fp-20261004-case-05-auditor1, independent attempt 1. Binding: `2074a79ca13cbb5c115db009fb5c9d64d60c5f86afade969e8ea17822b92fbbe`. Recipient: agentic-first-pass-20261004-lead. Authorized endpoint: research handoff only. Contract: 2026-09-27.3; research sidecar: causal-work-v1. Captures are dated 2026-10-04 UTC in individual receipts. Manifest SHA-256 was verified as `b171dad9b41cd294b99d3dd044b88bf45a4b11f3e2db60881ca6f618ead54189`.

## Finding

**NOT_AI under the frozen attribution threshold. The vulnerability itself is supported.** A verified ordinary user can persist their own chat history with cyclic string identifiers. Deleting a message can leave a cycle reachable by a synchronous, unguarded child-link descent. That descent cannot terminate, starving the affected worker's event loop. The default startup script runs one worker, supporting a default-deployment availability impact. This is a source-based conclusion, not an independently executed denial-of-service demonstration.

The smallest recovered causal change is `22a44e67a8ba781feb8f2a267fed0c40213d8432`, authored by Timothy Jaeryang Baek `<tim@openwebui.com>`. Its complete metadata has no AI disclosure. It introduces explicit message deletion and its traversal together. The contemporaneous PR template mentions AI review policy, but does not attribute this change to AI. All local commit objects were enumerated and the relevant historical path examined; AI-marked descendants carrying unchanged vulnerable content were separated from changes to that content or its exposure. No supported AI contribution to this defect was found. This protocol verdict does not claim to exclude undisclosed AI assistance.

The original repairing member is `2bd7f24d21591060e074a90f25df8bac087a2911`; its squash landing on `dev` is `b933292d63d12be3fd1416fe55519ddc7aa336bc`. First closure on the default branch is **`d3e8bf3405e848cfba377814d0aa7ba7290e414d`**, the 0.11.1 integration. These are distinct roles. Stable source tags 0.10.0, 0.10.1, 0.10.2 and 0.11.0 contain the identical unguarded helper; 0.11.1 contains the guard. The preceding 0.9.6 tag lacks the helper.

## Advisory identity and lifecycle

The keyed advisory is CVE-2026-88000. The live CVE record has matching `cveMetadata.cveId` and `state: PUBLISHED`; its CNA identifies open-webui and links GHSA-3cgp-3cqx-j8w2. The matching global GitHub advisory has `published_at: 2026-09-09T23:54:22Z` and explicit `withdrawn_at: null`, so both are ACTIVE. No withdrawn/rejected alias was observed. The retained NVD record says Analyzed, separately from publication lifecycle. Its version range agrees with the GHSA and CVE CNA.

Evidence: `sources/cve-current.json`, `sources/ghsa-current.json`, their paired `receipts/*.json` and HTTP headers; original assigned snapshots and provenance are copied as `sources/retained-*`. Fresh HTTP responses were successful. The GHSA description supplies the reported runtime measurements; this audit does not adopt them as its own measurements.

## Mechanism and authority

At affected repair-parent `f100edb70874808c93fab84eae1810595f9e9dc3`, `backend/open_webui/main.py:824` mounts the chats router at `/api/v1/chats`. `ChatForm` in `models/chats.py:230` accepts a dictionary, without a tree/acyclicity schema. The `/new` handler in `routers/chats.py:775` uses `get_verified_user`, then `Chats.insert_new_chat`. `utils/auth.py:497` allows roles `user` and `admin`. A folder-access check only applies when a folder is requested. No special privilege is needed for an ordinary user's own chat.

`insert_new_chat` at model line 492 stores a cleaned copy of the submitted dictionary, commits it, then performs a best-effort message-table dual write. Cleaning removes null bytes; it does not rebuild child links or enforce graph invariants. JSON represents this graph with message-ID strings, not recursive in-memory objects, so ordinary JSON serialization does not reject graph cycles. `merge_history` rebuilds child lists on an update path but is not used by creation. The persisted JSON remains the deletion helper's authoritative input; normalized message-table contents do not replace that input.

The `DELETE /{id}/messages/{message_id}` handler at router line 1497 loads the chat, checks owner or admin, and calls `delete_message_from_chat_by_id_and_message_id`. Ownership restricts whose chat can be modified but does not prevent a user from constructing the offending structure in their own chat. The model method at line 1101 sanitizes null bytes and calls `_repair_chat_current_id`, then synchronously calls `delete_message_from_history` at line 1113, inside the async request path. The current-ID repair does not validate or remove child-link cycles. Its optional `_last_descendant_id` walk is separately guarded; a normal valid current message without a context summary returns before that optional walk.

The deletion helper at lines 872–910 removes the selected message and its immediate children, reparents grandchildren, then starts at the removed message's parent and repeatedly follows the last child identifier. If that remaining relation leads back to an already visited message, the same finite state recurs forever: the loop neither mutates the remaining links nor records visits. This establishes the reported recurrence statically. A valid acyclic conversation instead ends at an empty child list. The invariant at issue is termination for every stored history reachable through an authorized product operation.

The spinning loop performs dictionary lookups and assignments with no await, cancellation checkpoint, allocation growth, or work budget. It therefore prevents the affected asyncio worker from handling other requests, including its health route. Existing request/session allocations stay live while CPU work continues; this is not a claim of growing memory use. The startup script defaults `UVICORN_WORKERS` to 1, also verified at the 0.11.0 source tag. Multiple-worker or replicated deployments require a narrower conclusion: one request blocks its selected worker; this inspection does not prove every worker or replica stalls. Request disconnects cannot be acted on by the blocked loop until it yields. The helper mutates an in-memory copy before database commit; a hang occurs before the deletion commit. The vulnerability claim is availability loss, not unauthorized disclosure. Ordinary successful deletion intentionally changes the user's chat.

Evidence: `sources/parent-chats.py`, `parent-router.py`, `parent-main.py`, `parent-auth.py`, `parent-start.sh`, `v0.11.0-start.sh`; each has a URL/HTTP/hash receipt. The reported exploit is retained only as original source evidence. No cyclic input was constructed or executed, and no application server or deployed target was contacted.

## Introduction, minimality and landing

The complete introducing patch is `sources/introduction.patch`; metadata and immediate parent are bound by `sources/introduction.json`, `receipts/introduction-search.txt`, and `receipts/final-observation-4.txt`. Parent: `24b8619f64731788ac38813768abbb64405effa4`.

The immediate parent has neither `delete_message_from_history` nor the explicit deletion endpoint. The child adds both, changes history updates to merge existing messages, and removes inference of deletion from omitted IDs. These are connected pieces of replacing implicit deletion with an explicit deletion operation, not unrelated features inferred to be atomic from file count. The unsafe descent is inside the newly introduced helper, and its newly added production caller makes the failure reachable in the same change. Thus ATOMIC is supported at the logical feature-change level. `sources/bic-parent-router.py` and `bic-router.py` establish caller differences; `receipts/final-observation-7.txt` is the local model parent/child diff. The previous parent's patch, `sources/bic-parent.patch`, does not contain the new walk.

The member landed on main through `4d2e13cf2bcc451b33bb6374bea4d2163e6cc94c` (PR 26385 / 0.10.0). The landing is not the introducer. Local ancestry and metadata are retained in `receipts/final-observations.json` and `final-observation-2.txt`; associated PR metadata is in `sources/introduction-prs.json`. Source extraction binds the member and landing to the identical helper SHA-256 `24566cb8b3ddc9941fbcb31d0fbe0739bfbefff526aa39dc9aec157ddb3f9502`. This is an actual function-content comparison, not attribution from a PR number. The repository is non-shallow; no root/import boundary or unreconstructable aggregate was needed.

## AI provenance and counterevidence

Full introducer metadata identifies Timothy Jaeryang Baek with a recoverable organization email and no AI marker. At that exact revision `.github/pull_request_template.md` says, “No Unchecked AI Code: This PR is either human-written or has undergone thorough human review AND manual testing.” This supports `POLICY_MENTIONS_AI`, not an inference that the patch was generated. The template is evidence only; its embedded contributor instructions were not adopted.

The local carrier inquiry used `git cat-file --batch-all-objects --batch-check`, covering 18,928 commit objects at initial enumeration, including any locally present unreachable objects. Tree traversal examined `backend/open_webui/models/chats.py`, found 165 distinct blobs, and read all 165 without missing content. There were 938 exact matches for the vulnerable helper. Every matching commit's complete metadata is retained in `receipts/carrier-metadata.txt`; the object/path universe, function digest and matches are in `receipts/local-object-universe.txt` and `carrier-analysis.json`. A later bounded repair-member fetch added exactly one commit, `2bd7f24d21591060e074a90f25df8bac087a2911`, whose full metadata and repairing patch were separately inspected; final enumeration is retained in `local-object-universe-final.txt`.

Twenty-four matches had AI-related marker candidates. Their full metadata and changed paths were inspected (`receipts/marker-scope.json` and individual `marker-*.txt`). They retain pre-existing vulnerable helper content while changing other operations. They do not attribute the original helper to AI merely by containing it. Two plausible indirect candidates received patch inspection: `c882222f68fed329705e028d4316f460b33b2cd0` adds ownership checks to chat-completed/actions, not to chat creation or message deletion; this case already requires ownership and therefore is not an omission of that ownership invariant. `8d6a7c8308c507f40466993732dbbd3c6930d04a` changes JSON engine serialization, preserving ordinary string-ID structure; it does not introduce graph acceptance that was previously prevented. See `sources/ai-ownership.patch` and `ai-json.patch`.

The separately cycle-guarded `_last_descendant_id` originated in `5caa91a49304148696641d1cd39e43184ba8d748`, also named Timothy Jaeryang Baek without an AI marker (`receipts/descendant-history.txt`, `sources/descendant-hardening.patch`). Its purpose/call site concerns selecting descendants for context-summary current messages. It does not repair the independent deletion walk, and its mere presence is not proof the deletion vulnerability was fixed earlier. No supported AI-attributed incomplete repair was found. Both the original repair member and its dev squash have no AI marker in their own complete metadata. Aggregate main-branch merge attribution is not assigned to a hunk.

Coverage is bounded to public primary material and the actual local object inventory, not inaccessible deleted remote history or private author activity. The promisor clone's configuration is disclosed, but all blobs in the enumerated historical causal path were present. No missing clone content was treated as evidence of no AI use.

## Repair and shipment

The minimum repair initializes `visited_ids`, checks the next identifier against it in the while condition, and adds each traversed identifier. With stable finite stored JSON, each existing identifier can be followed at most once; a missing child ends at an empty lookup. Malformed types may raise ordinary errors; this patch proves closure of the reported infinite cycle descent, not universal acceptance or sanitization of every malformed chat. The set has storage proportional to traversed identifiers. Surrounding deletion work still processes submitted child/grandchild lists, but there is no self-repeating traversal after this guard. Old stored cycles need no migration for this particular loop to terminate.

Original member `2bd7f24d21591060e074a90f25df8bac087a2911` and dev squash `b933292d63d12be3fd1416fe55519ddc7aa336bc` have the same repairing hunk (`sources/fix-member.patch`, `fix.patch`, associated commit and PR JSON). PR 28035 explicitly targeted dev. Default branch HEAD is main. Its first-parent history shows the 0.11.1 integration `d3e8bf3405e848cfba377814d0aa7ba7290e414d`, whose first parent `01f4282f1ffe0d6212f58d3afbeae21fffd0c4be` still has the vulnerable helper. Local diff and exact content show the integration closes the loop; ancestry separately shows the dev repair absent from the mainline parent and present at the integration. That negative ancestry result is exit 1 by design, not a retrieval failure.

`receipts/version-source-reads.json` records exact Git show commands, full commit and blob IDs, source hashes, and helper hashes for each compared revision and source tag. `sources/releases.json` supplies official tag names, publication dates, and prerelease flags. 0.11.1 is a stable release published 2026-08-25T21:17:57Z; its tag resolves to the main-branch integration. The guarded helper digest is `80276443b163f8d14b0137b8cba39b05f0549532c8793a71136f987336053065` at the dev repair, main integration and 0.11.1. The actual release router still invokes the repaired model method (`sources/release-router.py`), and release startup defaults retain the expected worker setup. Verified version claims concern these official source trees; this audit did not inspect every wheel, container, platform build or deployment.

An isolated ordinary regression check extracts only the helper AST from 0.11.0 and 0.11.1. Missing-message, leaf, middle, root and single-message deletions produce the same expected outputs before and after repair: ten assertions/checks passed. `receipts/ordinary-regression.txt` and its command receipt preserve the result. No cyclic histories, server execution, or exploit test occurred. Termination for cycles is a static proof from the guard, not a dynamic result.

## Failures, remaining questions and handoff

Execution failures are preserved separately from research findings. The initial history walk caused Git automatic packing to fail with “unable to create thread: Resource temporarily unavailable”; the raw `gc.log` is saved as `receipts/git-gc-failure.txt`. Auto-gc was disabled and pack threads limited to one in the owned scratch clone; the succeeding history query is retained. The initial noisy interactive query was not saved in full before tool-output truncation, so that exact full stdout is unavailable; this limitation is not hidden by the successful retry. Two broad `git show` attempts failed with exit 128 because lazy fetch was disabled and unrelated promisor blobs were missing (`receipts/introduction-object.*`, `ancestry-metadata.*`). Targeted local commit reads, causal-path diffs, and official raw/patch sources recovered the required evidence; the failures remain intact. The guessed `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` URL returned HTTP 404; a full source tree listing located the existing contemporary PR template instead. No rate limit, source access denial, or safety stop occurred.

No decisive causal question remains open within the stated public-source and source-release scope. The principal flip condition is a first-party disclosure or recovered member tying AI assistance to the introducing deletion logic, a later relevant exposure, or an attempted repair whose invariant actually includes this deletion path. An alternate parent/member changing the logical-atomicity finding, or an official released tree showing a different caller/guard, would also require revision. Merely finding an AI-marked unrelated descendant or a successful repair does not meet that condition. Runtime outage magnitude across every deployment and binary reproducibility were not asserted.

`record.json` is derived after this report. `research.json` records all six dimensions and their evidence boundaries. Strict structural and local-object checks, sidecar validation with frozen `check_research_work`, receipt hashes and a report/record readback are retained under `receipts/`; exact final stable-file hashes are in `SEAL.json`, excluding the seal itself. The leader owns subsequent acceptance and routing; no canonical, database, claims, deployment or publication changes were made.

The automatic IPP discovery SSRF mechanism is supported by version-matched source. The original exposure is attributable to a named human contribution under the frozen NOT_AI evidence threshold. A source-confirmed residual remains in both the claimed fixed 2026.2.3 source release and the latest stable release returned by the official release endpoint, 2026.9.4. ## Advisory status and scope

The keyed GHSA-4ghv-53cq-7wp3 is ACTIVE: both retained global REST data and the matching fresh REST response have published_at 2026-09-22T20:40:51Z and explicit withdrawn_at null. Neither is rejected or withdrawn. Sources: evidence/ghsa-live.json, cve-live.json, and the copied intake snapshots.

The advisory prose says prior to 2026.2.3, while its structured vulnerable_version_range says `< 2026.2.2` and first_patched_version says 2026.2.3. This inconsistency matters: direct source comparison establishes that 2026.2.2 still has the unguarded shared client. The report does not silently reconcile the structured range by trusting its label. The advisory's broad reference to internal services is also narrower than the implemented protection: RFC1918 destinations are not generically blocked.

## Causal mechanism and authority

In 2026.2.2, the IPP manifest registers `_ipp._tcp.local.` and `_ipps._tcp.local.` and pins pyipp 0.17.0. ZeroconfDiscovery matches the service to the integration and invokes discovery_flow.async_create_flow with SOURCE_ZEROCONF and the discovered service information. default_config includes zeroconf. Thus ordinary default discovery is a real product caller, not merely a test caller or dormant helper. Deployments without active zeroconf discovery are outside the automatic path.

IPPFlowHandler.async_step_zeroconf takes discovery_info.host and port, derives TLS from the service type, and derives base_path from the `rp` property. It checks already configured hosts/identifiers, then calls validate_input before async_step_zeroconf_confirm. Missing UUID is supported; an existing configured/ignored matching identity can abort before the probe. The attacker therefore needs local-network discovery reach and an accepted new discovery, not an authenticated Home Assistant account or prior IPP setup. Interactive confirmation occurs after the network operation.

The middleware wraps the response-returning handler inside aiohttp's redirect loop. retains complete metadata for the 500 matching vulnerable sanitizer carriers,
and records the object universe and inspected paths. Matching uses the srcdoc
allowlist hunk; exact blobs are recorded. The retained 33 contemporaneous commit

no observed AI disclosure convention. PR 614 reports zero comments/review comments.

generative-AI contribution. A later “improve llms docs” subject also supplies no

## Repair, shipment and limits

ec509a22c808a5bd9dfad6a0a85c92ce6f411e21 directly follows
67743149309054493ec8f5505173fc57aaff760f on the current default 9.x first-parent
history. It removes srcdoc from the actual shared sanitizer and adds a regression
expectation for removal. It also requires RAW_HTML to be enabled before selecting
the data-html-content preservation route. This second hunk matters to the intended
ordinary-input boundary, even though direct iframe removal needs only the first.
No separate merge is the first default-branch closure. Tests, EditorFormatter
wiring, and the sibling TextFormatter use the shared implementation; the fix is
not an unused helper change. Explicit RAW_HTML is documented as unsanitized.

Official release metadata, not guessed tag URLs, identifies v9.22.5 as stable,
created 2026-06-24T11:59:08Z, published 2026-06-24T12:01:02Z. Its tag resolves to
4a3973c0bc4ee64f1eb57db9713b8668b591e88a, with repaired sanitizer blob
14f7de5236f8b7357ed3eea55368dfb6802a989f. v9.22.4's source has the vulnerable blob;
its release was published 2026-06-24T12:00:39Z despite a June 8 created_at.

sanitizer and was published 2025-08-22T13:26:17Z. Source comparisons, not tag
ancestry alone, substantiate these findings. The current 9.x tip still omits srcdoc
from that allowlist. No binary, deployment or every historical release was verified.

The repair does not sanitize on toFront and does not migrate an application's
persisted content. Users handling already-untrusted saved values need cleanup or
an effective rendering sanitizer; intentional RAW_HTML/disabled sanitization and
custom embed trust must be assessed separately. Those limits are outside the
bounded prospective allowlist closure claimed here. This report does not certify
all security invariants of the special embed preservation mechanism.

Evidence: intro-repair.txt, mainline-history.txt, release-metadata.txt,
causal-chain.txt, source-checks.txt, final-source-comparisons.txt.

# Independent research: code16/sharp iframe srcdoc

Task: agentic-fp-20261004-case-06-auditor1, independent attempt 1. Class:
alias-fdf82fc73934d0a1a7056a52. Binding:
16eda5845d6300ef9a4f006ba3d90130e5fdc8a641c972d30a6f0af4049c8cb6.
Recipient: agentic-first-pass-20261004-lead; research handoff only.
Contract: 2026-09-27.3; research-work: causal-work-v1. Research date: 2026-10-04 UTC.

## Finding and scope

The stored-XSS mechanism is supported by primary source inspection. The specific
sanitizer regression is a named-human change with no admitted causal AI marker:
**NOT_AI under the frozen protocol's bounded attribution threshold**. This does
not establish that the author never used undisclosed tools. It does not reject the
advisory. The independently demonstrated scope is ordinary HTML Editor input
processed through the enabled server sanitizer, subsequently rendered by a
configured iframe-capable Editor or an application HTML consumer without an
additional effective sanitizer. The default minimal Editor toolbar does not
contain iframe, and the default Sharp Show text renderer has a separate client
sanitizer. Those distinctions limit exposure, rather than negate the server defect.

The atomic sanitizer regression is bafa8c41be4696285059c19d61b9bea61a31db00
(2025-08-07), carried by ca9dfaa96afd3686053d37123ce25fc728c89b21 (PR 614).
The ordinary incoming-iframe repair is ec509a22c808a5bd9dfad6a0a85c92ce6f411e21
(2026-06-24), present as actual source content in stable v9.22.5. The repair is
prospective input sanitization: it neither rewrites an application's old database
values nor promises to sanitize explicitly trusted RAW_HTML, custom embeds, or
fields configured with sanitization disabled. Do not translate this finding into
an assertion that upgrading alone makes previously poisoned persisted content safe.

## Advisory identity and freshness

The manifest bytes hash to the bound
054b8f9c816e8d18e2bbef31ff6a8579d08537a284d523ff3cc14f36ccb8792b.
Both retained input objects match SOURCES.json hashes (receipts/source-checks.txt).
The keyed official advisory here is GHSA-qxg3-46rw-79j8; CVE-2026-61823 is its
explicit alias. The refreshed matching global GitHub response is HTTP 200,
published_at 2026-09-25T15:02:11Z, withdrawn_at null, hence ACTIVE. The matching
CVE API response is HTTP 200 with cveMetadata.state PUBLISHED, hence ACTIVE.
The earlier NVD snapshot's Received is processing status, not a rejection.
The retained and current GHSA agree on the mechanism, package, repair object and
claimed range <9.22.5. Publication is distinct from the June repair/release dates.

Evidence: receipts/remote-advisory.txt, receipts/cve-current.txt,
sources/00-github.json, sources/01-nvd.json, receipts/causal-chain.txt.
Each network receipt retains the exact URL, capture times, curl exit and HTTP
headers. The receipt field `repository` identifies the investigated product;
the URL identifies the actual authority for Symfony, WHATWG and CVE responses.

## Causal chain and counterevidence

At v9.22.4 (5c36e853e364cb117602038b3b3a9306baaf8928), FormController::update
checks update authorization before passing request data into
formatAndValidateRequestData. Store checks creation authorization. HandleFormFields
filters declared data keys and invokes the configured field formatter. Legacy
validators may run before formatting; ordinary rules run on formatted values.
Neither a successful authorization check nor string/length validation makes HTML
safe. The application-specific update callback owns persistence. The repository's
PostForm demonstrates a real configured HTML Editor with IFRAME, localized content,
ordinary string rules, and save($post, $data); this is source evidence, not a live
demo interaction or a claim that all applications use that model.

EditorFormatter::fromFront accepts a string or a `text` value, normalizes newlines,
and calls sanitizeHtmlIfNeeded through maybeLocalized. SharpFormEditorField enables
sanitizeHtml by default. For ordinary iframe HTML the trait reaches HtmlSanitizer
without the embeds/RAW_HTML preservation detour. Its allowElement('iframe', ...)
explicitly admits srcdoc, but does not impose a sandbox. The default Symfony 7.3.0
configuration has a URL sanitizer for src, href, lowsrc, background and ping, not
srcdoc. DomVisitor copies allowed values; Node::renderAttributes entity-encodes
them. Encoding a nested document as an attribute preserves its eventual document
semantics; it is not recursive sanitization of that document.

On later edit/readback, EditorFormatter::toFront returns stored text without calling
the server sanitizer. Editor.vue feeds it into the editor instance. The iframe
extension is enabled when toolbarHas('iframe'); it parses all attributes except
onload/onerror and passes them to IframeNode.vue's actual iframe through v-bind.
There is no forced sandbox in that node. WHATWG's iframe specification establishes
that srcdoc is an inline document; escaping attribute delimiters does not convert
that document into inert text. This supplies a source-level path from an authorized
editor's persisted value to another authorized user's browser. A field need not
enable RAW_HTML for this path. The default toolbar (bold, italic, list, link) does
not itself activate the iframe node, so “every Editor viewer” would overstate it.

The relevant invariant is that ordinary sanitized Editor content must not retain
an attacker-controlled executable nested document. Same-origin script execution
can act with the viewing user's browser authority where no effective CSP or sandbox
prevents it. The advisory's document.cookie/session theft example is conditional:
HttpOnly cookies are not readable by script. No deployment cookie policy, CSP,
actual session compromise, or observed exploitation is asserted here.

SharpShowTextField defaults sanitize=true; Text.vue invokes DOMPurify via sanitize.ts
before rendering HTML. That helper adds iframe but does not expressly add srcdoc.
This is an additional defensive layer, not evidence that the vulnerable server
allowlist is harmless. No browser execution was performed, and no broad claim that
all Show configurations execute this content is made. External HTML consumers and
explicitly disabled sanitization have application-specific behavior.

Decisive receipts: caller-chain.txt, caller-search-retry.txt,
final-source-comparisons.txt, source-checks.txt, symfony-config.txt,
symfony-visitor.txt, symfony-url-filter.txt, symfony-node-corrected.txt,
html-standard.txt. Extracted affected files are in sources/v9.22.4/ with blob
identities in source-extraction.txt. These are static observations and causal
inference; upstream regression-test source was inspected, not executed.

## Introduction, earlier exposure and landing

The immediate parent dc8be08ad86432970680d181ffa315d4ce0ce3bb has sanitizer blob
2a38dcbc1266b1d56ab69244c165393e2c57de61 and allowElement('iframe') with no
attributes. Symfony allowElement resets that element's permitted attributes to
the supplied list. The child bafa8c41 introduces blob
cc5d66188222a5aad3511391fc3414b5f633fd39, adding iframe attributes including
srcdoc. EditorFormatter and iframe frontend blobs are unchanged across this edge.
Thus under identical input and enabled sanitization the parent removes srcdoc and
the child retains it. This isolates the server regression rather than relying on
a pickaxe hit alone.

The change consists of one iframe-compatibility policy and its corresponding
formatter-test adjustments. It is logically atomic at that feature/policy level;
its two files are not the argument for atomicity. The minimum causal hunk is
the added srcdoc entry. PR 614 is a broader sanitization integration containing
12 commits; the report does not attribute its whole bundle to this hunk.
The landed sanitizer blob equals the bafa8c41 child blob exactly. The merge's
mainline parent lacks this new sanitizer, so the member regression and mainline
integration are distinct roles. No member-recovery fetch was needed: all members
and their trees are available in the non-shallow, non-promisor owned clone.

This is not the first time Sharp could store unsafe HTML. The earlier
738af7d6b6e7659ef2ce9abce02a9878245e71c7 (2025-04-17) changes the iframe frontend
from a fixed attribute schema to arbitrary attributes except two handlers. Its
parent/child diff supports an earlier editor exposure change. v9.6.0's
EditorFormatter has no sanitizeHtmlIfNeeded call; v9.7.0's release announces
server sanitization as a new default. 07e60698816259a5dfd92135396d6bea334ad8b2
introduced that sanitization on the feature branch, followed by a move and then
bafa8c41's relaxation. Accordingly bafa8c41 is the precise origin of the advisory's
faulty sanitizer allowance, not a claim to the first unsafe HTML behavior anywhere
in older Sharp. The older change is human-authored without an AI marker; the
full historical lower affected bound for all rendering modes is not established.

Evidence: intro-repair.txt, earlier-sanitization.txt, earlier-exposure.txt,
iframe-history.txt, mainline-history.txt, causal-chain.txt, source-checks.txt.

## AI evidence and admissibility

bafa8c41's raw identity is antoine <guingand.antoine@gmail.com>. The GitHub commit
response binds it to aguingand (User); the package composer metadata names Antoine
Guingand. Its full commit message is “Fix iframe”, without an AI disclosure.
The repairing commit independently has the same human email identity and no AI
marker. A human name alone was not used as proof of absent AI participation.

The clone's cat-file --batch-all-objects universe contains 7,218 commit objects.
For each, the carrier audit resolves the sanitizer path and EditorFormatter path,
retains complete metadata for the 500 matching vulnerable sanitizer carriers,
and records the object universe and inspected paths. Matching uses the srcdoc
allowlist hunk; exact blobs are recorded. The retained 33 contemporaneous commit
messages (2025-08-01 through 2025-08-23), BIC-era README and PR 614 metadata contain
no observed AI disclosure convention. PR 614 reports zero comments/review comments.
Convention classification: CONVENTION_NOT_OBSERVED at the BIC date.

AI-related evidence does exist elsewhere: five later Copilot-trailered commits
and a generator merge with a codex branch name inherit the vulnerable sanitizer
blob. Their first-parent comparisons have the identical sanitizer blob and change
authentication documentation or generator code/tests. These markers do not
attribute the inherited sanitizer hunk, its introduction or its exposure. StyleCI
trailers in earlier history identify formatting automation, not demonstrated
generative-AI contribution. A later “improve llms docs” subject also supplies no
causal authorship disclosure. No accepted marker binds to a causal introducing,
exposing, or deficient-hardening change found in this investigation.

The carrier coverage is local-object coverage, including any unreferenced objects
actually delivered in the clone. It cannot prove that unknown private or unfetched
force-push iterations never existed. A first-party disclosure tied by exact content
to the causal change would change this conclusion. Evidence: intro-api.txt,
intro-pr.txt, carriers.json, object-universe.txt, carrier-audit.txt,
marker-diffs.txt, source-checks.txt, broader-marker-check.txt.

## Repair, shipment and limits

ec509a22c808a5bd9dfad6a0a85c92ce6f411e21 directly follows
67743149309054493ec8f5505173fc57aaff760f on the current default 9.x first-parent
history. It removes srcdoc from the actual shared sanitizer and adds a regression
expectation for removal. It also requires RAW_HTML to be enabled before selecting
the data-html-content preservation route. This second hunk matters to the intended
ordinary-input boundary, even though direct iframe removal needs only the first.
No separate merge is the first default-branch closure. Tests, EditorFormatter
wiring, and the sibling TextFormatter use the shared implementation; the fix is
not an unused helper change. Explicit RAW_HTML is documented as unsanitized.

Official release metadata, not guessed tag URLs, identifies v9.22.5 as stable,
created 2026-06-24T11:59:08Z, published 2026-06-24T12:01:02Z. Its tag resolves to
4a3973c0bc4ee64f1eb57db9713b8668b591e88a, with repaired sanitizer blob
14f7de5236f8b7357ed3eea55368dfb6802a989f. v9.22.4's source has the vulnerable blob;
its release was published 2026-06-24T12:00:39Z despite a June 8 created_at.
v9.7.0 (b35b76e28c7a01accf2d288f189987bcf9998170) also contains the vulnerable
sanitizer and was published 2025-08-22T13:26:17Z. Source comparisons, not tag
ancestry alone, substantiate these findings. The current 9.x tip still omits srcdoc
from that allowlist. No binary, deployment or every historical release was verified.

The repair does not sanitize on toFront and does not migrate an application's
persisted content. Users handling already-untrusted saved values need cleanup or
an effective rendering sanitizer; intentional RAW_HTML/disabled sanitization and
custom embed trust must be assessed separately. Those limits are outside the
bounded prospective allowlist closure claimed here. This report does not certify
all security invariants of the special embed preservation mechanism.

Evidence: intro-repair.txt, mainline-history.txt, release-metadata.txt,
causal-chain.txt, source-checks.txt, final-source-comparisons.txt.

affected releases, fix parent/child, fixed release and present default branch.

## Finding

**NOT_AI under the frozen bounded attribution threshold.** The active advisory
describes a real sanitizer defect. Its atomic iframe-allowance regression is
human-identified and lacks an admissible causal AI disclosure. This conclusion
does not establish universal absence of undisclosed AI use.

direct allowlist repair, but neither establishes closure across the Editor's
preservation path. Independent inspection finds that v9.22.5 and the retained
current 9.x head still restore selected input nodes after sanitization without
enforcing RAW_HTML permission at the node-selection step. Another encoding
sentinel can select that path even with RAW_HTML disabled. This is a source-bound
remaining surface for the same iframe content, rather than merely old database
content or intentional RAW_HTML. No full closing commit was found in the complete
retained relevant-path history or the fresh default-branch source. Accordingly,
the synthesis does not claim a fully patched release. The advertised v9.22.5
patch is supported specifically for the direct, non-preserved iframe path.

This is static source and standards analysis. No exploit, payload, browser
execution or deployed-target interaction was performed.

## Advisory and input integrity

The manifest matches SHA256
054b8f9c816e8d18e2bbef31ff6a8579d08537a284d523ff3cc14f36ccb8792b.
All 165 auditor1 and 16 auditor2 sealed payload files match their seals;
both retained advisory snapshots match SOURCES.json. The original record paths
are used for comparison and reduction, with their exact bytes pinned.

Fresh first-party HTTP 200 responses independently establish the keyed
GHSA-qxg3-46rw-79j8 as published at 2026-09-25T15:02:11Z with withdrawn_at null,
and CVE-2026-61823 as PUBLISHED. The GHSA explicitly links that CVE and identifies
composer package code16/sharp, affected range <9.22.5 and first patched 9.22.5.
NVD processing states are not withdrawal evidence. The advisory's repair claim
is kept separate from the code-derived qualification below.

Receipts: evidence/integrity.json, current-ghsa.json/.txt/.headers/.receipt.json,
current-cve.json/.txt/.headers/.receipt.json.

## Trigger, caller, stored representation and recipient

At v9.22.4 an authorized Editor writer submits text. FormController checks
create/update authorization; HandleFormFields formats declared fields, and the
application's save callback persists the result. EditorFormatter::fromFront
reaches FormatsSanitizedValue with sanitization enabled by default. The shared
HtmlSanitizer configuration allows iframe srcdoc without requiring a sandbox.
The retained first-party Symfony 7.3.0 implementation copies allowed attributes
and HTML-encodes them on output; its URL-attribute sanitizer does not target
srcdoc. This serializes the nested document rather than recursively sanitizing
it. WHATWG's iframe definition establishes the inline-document semantics.

EditorFormatter::toFront does not run that sanitizer on saved text. The Editor's
iframe extension, when IFRAME is configured, parses attributes except the two
event handlers it explicitly excludes and binds them onto a real iframe. There
is no mandatory sandbox. Script-capable nested content can therefore cross from
writer-controlled stored text to a viewer's origin authority, subject to effective
CSP and other application protections. Cookie theft additionally requires
script-readable cookies. No actual session compromise is claimed.

The repository PostForm supplies an actual iframe-enabled Editor/save example.
The minimal default toolbar lacks IFRAME, and default Show text uses a separate
DOMPurify sanitizer. Those are exposure qualifications, not refutation of the
server defect. Broad claims about every Editor or Show configuration are rejected.

Primary receipts: evidence/callers.txt and versions.txt; retained auditor1
receipts/symfony-config.txt, symfony-visitor.txt, symfony-url-filter.txt,
symfony-node-corrected.txt and html-standard.txt. Their full hashes are pinned
in decisions.json and the research sidecar.

coherent iframe attribute-compatibility policy, including srcdoc, and associated
formatter-test changes. Immediate parent dc8be08ad86432970680d181ffa315d4ce0ce3bb
allows iframe with an empty attribute list. Symfony allowElement resets that
list. Unchanged formatter/frontend context therefore isolates the allowance as
the regression. Granularity is ATOMIC for this policy; a single parent or two
changed files alone would not establish that judgment.

The landed sanitizer blob cc5d66188222a5aad3511391fc3414b5f633fd39 equals the
member's blob. ca9dfaa96afd3686053d37123ce25fc728c89b21 integrates the feature
through PR 614; its mainline parent lacks the new sanitizer. It is the distinct
carrier, not the atomic introducer. Full objects are available in the non-shallow
retained auditor1 repository, with no configured promisor/partial clone.

sanitizer call, and human-authored 738af7d6b6e7659ef2ce9abce02a9878245e71c7 had

in the human-authored sanitization work 07e60698816259a5dfd92135396d6bea334ad8b2,
before the iframe relaxation, and is retained as a distinct related origin.

residual-chain.txt and versions.txt.

ec509a22c808a5bd9dfad6a0a85c92ce6f411e21 directly follows
67743149309054493ec8f5505173fc57aaff760f on 9.x. Its atomic direct repair removes
srcdoc and adds an expected-output regression. Its other relevant hunk gates the
data-html-content *trigger* on RAW_HTML. This is prospective input repair;
toFront still does not clean already-persisted values.

The decisive counterevidence is the mismatch between trigger selection and node
selection. isEncodingNeeded still tests unconditional upload-marker substrings
and configured embed names. Once any such sentinel selects encoding,
encodeEmbedsAndRawHtml tests each top-level DOMElement for a configured embed
tag, any x-prefixed tag, **or presence of data-html-content**. The last test is
not gated on RAW_HTML. It serializes the selected node into a permitted
data-encoded-content attribute, so the sanitizer sees the transport container,
not that node's original iframe attributes. decodeEmbedsAndRawHtml parses and
restores that serialized node after the sanitizer has finished. No sanitizer is
run on the restored document. The internal decoding attribute is also accepted
without provenance validation; no comprehensive safety guarantee for that
transport follows from removing srcdoc on ordinary visible iframes.

For a field without uploads or custom embeds, both subsequent formatters return
the text unchanged; their afterUpdate paths likewise do not apply an HTML
sanitizer. Thus upload/RAW_HTML configuration is not a mandatory downstream guard
for this branch. The existing iframe reader can still consume a restored iframe.
The observation is a static branch analysis, not an executed exploit or supplied
input recipe. It refutes the auditors' complete prospective ordinary-input
closure. Auditor1's explicit exclusion of “custom embed trust” does not address
the unconditional sentinel path for a field with no configured embeds/uploads.
